hook_text: In 1854, a doctor stopped a deadly outbreak by removing the handle of a water pump.
clip_script: London, 1854. Cholera is killing hundreds of people in a few days. Most doctors blame bad air. John Snow thinks differently. He marks every death on a map, and they cluster around one water pump on Broad Street. He has the handle removed, and the new cases fall away. Sewage in drinking water was the killer. Cities started building sewers and clean water supplies. Add vaccines, germ theory, antibiotics, canned food and fridges, and suddenly far fewer children died. That is a big reason why the world's population took off.
visual_style: An old street map fills with black bars around a pump; a hand removes the pump handle; the scene shifts to sewer tunnels, a vaccine, a tin can and a fridge in quick succession.
pacing: A slow mystery build, a click as the handle comes off, then a quick montage.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson on scientific developments and population.
